hr.tip.old: The port is probably not the API Server, or Holyrics is older than 2.21: update Holyrics and take the port from File → Settings → API Server.

hr.tip.net: Check: phone and computer on the same Wi-Fi; API Server enabled in Holyrics (File → Settings → API Server) and the port taken from there — not the Holyrics mobile app port; Windows Firewall allows Holyrics (Allow an app → Holyrics/Java, private networks); the address is the computer’s IPv4 (ipconfig), not 127.0.0.1.

hr.hint: In Holyrics: File → Settings → API Server — enable the server; the address and port are shown there (the API Server has its own port, not the one of the Holyrics mobile app); “Manage permissions” — create a token with the GetSongs permission. Phone and computer on the same Wi-Fi. “Check” — connection and token without loading songs. Connections happen only via these buttons and only to this address.

report.title: Report a problem
report.intro: A report helps find a bug even when it is hard to describe. It contains what happened, device details and a technical log of the last 3 hours. It has no song or file names, texts, name, camera frames or sound. The app never sends anything by itself: the report is sent via Share — for example, to Telegram or by email.

bg.title: Background work
bg.text: So that practice, the metronome, pads, media and timers do not stop when the app is minimised or the screen is off, Android needs to allow background work. While something runs, a “Melete” line is shown in the notification shade.
bg.hint: On Honor, Huawei, Xiaomi and some other phones, App settings also need: Battery → “App launch” (or “Autostart”) → allow background activity. In the background the app sends and records nothing.
bg.featHint: While practice runs or an instrument sounds, the app keeps working in the background.

tos.title: Before you start
tos.p1: The app is free and has no ads. Microphone sound is processed on the device only and is never sent anywhere.
tos.p2: Everything you add yourself — recordings, tabs, lyrics — stays on your device and is your responsibility. Only add things you have the rights to.

stone.title: Stone
stone.path: travelled — how far a pebble rolls down a river to wear this smooth (50 m per hour of practice)
stone.text: An ordinary stone from the road. Every hour of practice in the app wears it down, like a stone kicked and rolled for years: sharp edges smooth out first (the first hundreds of hours), then chips and bumps go and it becomes a rounded version of itself (thousands of hours), and slowest of all it grows round — almost a ball after tens of thousands of hours. The stone can be turned with a finger.

The engine includes TensorFlow Lite, XNNPACK, OpenCV, Protocol Buffers and Abseil (Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause). Modified: the built-in usage statistics collector that sent data to Google has been removed. Tracking runs only on the device.

guard.hint: On many phones a three-finger touch takes a screenshot, turning a chord on the piano or pads into a screenshot. While the piano, glider or pads are open, screenshots are blocked — and screen recording pauses too (this is how Android works). In other instruments and on all app screens screenshots and screen recording work. To record playing the piano, turn this protection off here. The gesture itself can also be turned off in the phone settings (Gestures → Three-finger screenshot).
